questionText:
In the question below, a statement followed by two conclusions numbered I and II is given. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true, then consider the two conclusions together and decide which of them logically follows beyond a reasonable doubt from the information given in the statement.
Statement : If all players play to their full potential, we will win the match. We have won the match.
Conclusions :
I. All players played to their full potential.
II. Some players did not play to their full potential.
solution:
Solution

Given:
Statement: If all players play to their full potential, we will win the match. We have won the match.

Conclusions:

I. All players played to their full potential - False (Because the
statement is of the form If P, then Q. From the fact that Q has occurred (we won the match), it cannot be concluded that P (all players played to their full potential) must have occurred. The team could have won for other reasons.)

II. Some players did not play to their full potential - False (Because there is no information to conclude that any player failed to play to their full potential. This is also not logically implied by the statement.)

So, neither
Conclusion I nor
Conclusion II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

solution:
Solution

Assertion

The earliest Ajanta caves were carved in the 2nd Century BC out of a horse-shoe-shaped cliffs along the Waghora River.
They were used by Buddhist monks as prayer halls (chaitya grihas) and monasteries (viharas) for about nine centuries.

REASON

Out of the 30 excavated caves, five (cave no. 9, 10, 19, 26, and 29) are chaitya grihas (prayer halls) and the rest are viharas (monasteries).
In date and style, these caves can be divided into two broad phases.
Phase I (2nd Century to 1st Century BCE) - The earliest excavations were done by the Satavahanas and belong to the Hinayana (Theravada) phase of Buddhism. The object of worship is a stupa here. Caves 9, 10, 12, 13 and 15A belong to this era.
Phase II (5th Century AD to 6th Century AD) - These excavations are a major contribution of the Vakatakas and Chalukyas and belong to Mahayana phase of Buddhism which is mostly a Post Gupta age.

Cave 1 is a magnificently painted Vihara (monastery), filled with wall murals, sculptures, and ceiling paintings, that date back to the 5th century. Originally, Cave 1 also had a porch that led to the main hall, however, it has since collapsed.

Cave 2  was started in the 460s but mostly carved between 475 and 477 CE, probably sponsored and influenced by a woman closely related to emperor Harisena. It has a porch quite different from Cave 1. Even the façade carvings seem to be different. The cave is supported by robust pillars, ornamented with designs. The front porch consists of cells supported by pillared vestibules on both ends.

Fill in the blanks by choosing the appropriate option.
Milk ........... Ensures that Vitamins (A/D) reach consumers who buy low-fat milk.
solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Fortification.

Key Points
Food Fortification:
Fortification is the addition of key vitamins and minerals such as Iron, Iodine, Zinc, Vitamins A & D to staple foods such as rice, wheat, oil, milk and salt to improve their nutritional content.
These nutrients may or may not have been originally present in the food before processing or may have been lost during processing.
Why do we Need the Fortification of Food?
Deficiency of micronutrients or micronutrient malnutrition, also known as hidden hunger, is a serious health risk.
Access to safe and nutritious food is a must and sometimes due to lack of consumption of a balanced diet, lack of variety in the diet or unavailability of food one does not get adequate micronutrients. Often, there is a considerable loss of nutrients during the processing of food as well.
One of the strategies to address this problem is the fortification of food.
This method complements other ways to improve nutrition such as diversification of diet and supplementation of food.

Additional Information
Standardization
The adjustment of one or more of the milk constituents to meet the legal requirement or nominated level.
In the market milk industry, normally involves reducing the butterfat content by the addition of skim milk or. Through the removal of the cream.

Pasteurization
Pasteurized milk is a raw milk that has been heated to a specified temperature and time to kill pathogens that may be found in the raw milk.
Pathogens are microorganisms such as bacteria that make humans sick. Raw milk can contain pathogens such as Campylobacter, E. coli, Salmonella, Listeria, and other bacteria.

Homogenization
Homogenization is a mechanical process used to reduce the size of the fat globules in the milk.
Reduce the milk fat globules size to less than 1.0 μm which allows them to stay evenly distributed in milk.
Homogenization is a high-pressure process that forces milk at a high velocity through a small orifice to break up the globules.

questionText: Which mountain range runs from northwest to southeast and forms a natural boundary between the Kashmir valley and the outer plains?
solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Pir Panjal Range.

Key Points
The Pir Panjal Range is part of the Inner Himalayan region and runs from northwest to southeast, forming a natural boundary between the Kashmir Valley and the outer plains.
This range separates the Kashmir Valley from the lesser Himalayan regions and lies south of the main Himalayan range.
It is known for its significant mountain passes like the Pir Panjal Pass, Banihal Pass, and Rohtang Pass, which have been crucial for trade and travel.
The range is home to dense forests and is rich in biodiversity, contributing significantly to the ecology of the region.
The Pir Panjal Range is also known for its beautiful landscapes and is a popular destination for trekking and tourism in India.

Additional Information
Karakoram Range
The Karakoram Range lies to the north of the Himalayan Range and forms the border between India, Pakistan, and China.
It is home to some of the world’s highest peaks, including K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen), the second-highest peak in the world.
The Siachen Glacier, the largest glacier in India, is located in the Karakoram Range.
Known for its rugged terrain and harsh climate, the region has a sparse population.
Ladakh Range
The Ladakh Range lies to the north of the Zanskar Range and runs parallel to it.
This range is a part of the Trans-Himalayas and is located in the Union Territory of Ladakh.
Famous for its arid, barren landscapes and high-altitude passes, it plays a crucial role in Ladakh’s topography.
Popular passes in this range include Khardung La and Chang La, which are among the highest motorable passes in the world.
Dhauladhar Range
The Dhauladhar Range is part of the Lesser Himalayas and lies to the south of the Pir Panjal Range.
It is known for its steep slopes and sharp ridges and is prominent in the Kangra Valley region of Himachal Pradesh.
It serves as a prominent tourist destination and is home to numerous trekking routes.
Triund, a popular trekking spot, is located in the Dhauladhar Range.

solution:
Solution

The correct answer is March 1946
Key Points
Cabinet Mission:

The Cabinet Mission came to India with the objective to discuss the transfer of powers from the British government to the Indian leadership.
The aim is to safeguard India's unity and grant its independence.
Cabinet Mission was a high-powered mission sent by the Atlee Government (British Prime Minister) that arrived in India in 24th March 1946.
The mission had three British cabinet members - Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, & and A.V. Alexander.
Clement Atlee (British Prime Minister) decided to send a mission to India for the transfer of powers from the British Indian government to Indian leaders.

Additional Information
Objectives:

To obtain an agreement with the Indian leaders as to the framing of a constitution for India.
To formulate a constitution-making body (the Constituent Assembly of India).
To establish an Executive Council with the support of the major Indian parties.

Reason for failure:

The Congress Party wanted a strong centre with minimum powers for the provinces.
The Muslim League wanted strong political safeguards for the Muslims like parity in the legislatures.
Since both parties had many ideological differences and could not find common ground, the mission came up with its own set of proposals in May 1946.

solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Mahavansh.

Key Points
The Mahavansh is a historical chronicle of Sri Lanka, written in Pali.
It provides a detailed account of the rulers of ancient Sri Lanka, including their contributions to Buddhism and governance.
The text mentions that Ashoka was appointed as the ruler of Avanti by his father, Emperor Bindusara, at the age of 18.
The Mahavansh is considered an important source of historical information for early Buddhist history and the spread of Buddhism in the region.
This chronicle is divided into multiple chapters, detailing various dynasties, events, and rulers.

Additional Information
Ashoka the Great:
Ashoka was the third emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, ruling from 268 BCE to 232 BCE.
He played a key role in spreading Buddhism across India and other regions, including Central Asia.
He is known for his policy of Dhamma, promoting peace, tolerance, and welfare of all living beings.
The Edicts of Ashoka are inscriptions carved on rocks and pillars, showcasing his policies and principles.
Avanti Region:
Avanti was an important kingdom in ancient India, corresponding to modern-day Madhya Pradesh.
The capital cities of Avanti were Ujjain and Mahishmati.
It played a significant role in ancient Indian trade, culture, and politics.
Avanti later became a part of the Maurya Empire under Ashoka's administration.
Mahavansh's Historical Significance:
The Mahavansh is a continuation of the Dipavansh, another historical chronicle of Sri Lanka.
It provides insights into the reigns of Sri Lankan rulers, Buddhist history, and relations with Indian kingdoms.
The text is highly revered in Sri Lankan culture and serves as a vital resource for historians and scholars.
Spread of Buddhism:
Ashoka's efforts led to the propagation of Buddhism within and beyond India.
He sent missionaries to regions such as Sri Lanka, Central Asia, and Southeast Asia.
The Mahavansh records King Devanampiya Tissa of Sri Lanka adopting Buddhism under Ashoka's influence.

questionText: A crop primarily associated with equatorial regions can also be cultivated in tropical and sub-tropical areas. It requires a hot and humid climate, annual rainfall exceeding 200 cm, and temperatures generally above 25°C. Which one of the following crops fits this description?
solution:
Solution
The correct answer is Option B.

Key Points
The crop described requires a hot and humid climate, very high rainfall (over 200 cm), and consistently high temperatures (above 25°C)-conditions typical of equatorial regions, but also found in parts of the tropics and sub-tropics.
Rubber is primarily an equatorial crop, thriving in regions with uniformly high temperatures, heavy and well-distributed rainfall, and high humidity. Hence, Option B is correct.

questionText: From 11 to 50, how many numbers are there which are exactly divisible by 7 but not by 3?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total multiples of 7 from 11 to 50 = (Largest multiple - Smallest multiple) ÷ 7 + 1 = (49 - 14) ÷ 7 + 1 = 6.

Total multiples of 21 (divisible by both 7 and 3) from 11 to 50 = (42 - 21) ÷ 21 + 1 = 2.

Total numbers divisible by 7 but not by 3 = 6 - 2 = 4.
∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.

Alternate Method
Given:
Range of numbers: From 11 to 50.
Condition: Numbers must be divisible by 7 but not by 3.

Calculations:
⇒ First, list all the numbers between 11 and 50 that are exactly divisible by 7.
⇒ These multiples are: 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49.
⇒ Total count of these multiples = 6.
⇒ Next, identify the numbers from this list that are also divisible by 3.
⇒ A number divisible by both 7 and 3 must be divisible by their LCM, which is 21.
⇒ The multiples of 21 in the given range are: 21 and 42.
⇒ We must exclude these 2 numbers from our initial list.
⇒ The remaining numbers are: 14, 28, 35, 49.
⇒ Total count of the remaining numbers = 4.
∴ The correct answer is 4 numbers.

Additional Information
LCM of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime (like 3 and 7, having no common factors other than 1), their Least Common Multiple (LCM) is simply their product (3 × 7 = 21). Any number divisible by both must be a multiple of this LCM.

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Counting

To find the number of terms in an AP, you can use the formula: Number of terms = (Last term - First term) ÷ Common Difference + 1.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is exactly divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

questionText: The length of a room is 5.5 m and the width is 3.75 m. Find the cost of paving the floor with slabs at the rate of Rs. 800 per sq. meter.
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total Cost = Length × Width × Rate per m2
Cost = 5.5 × 3.75 × 800

Multiply 3.75 by 800 first: 3.75 × 800 = 3000

Cost = 5.5 × 3000 = 16500
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 16500.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length of the room (L) = 5.5 m
Width of the room (W) = 3.75 m
Rate of paving = Rs. 800 per m2

Formula Used:
Area of a rectangle = Length × Width
Total Cost = Area × Rate per unit area

Calculations:
⇒ Area of the floor = 5.5 m × 3.75 m
⇒ Area = 20.625 m2
⇒ Total Cost = 20.625 × 800
⇒ Total Cost = 16500
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 16500.

Additional Information
Area of Rectangle

The total space enclosed within the boundaries of a rectangle. Formula: Area = Length × Breadth.

Perimeter of Rectangle

The total length of the boundary of a rectangle. Formula: Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth). This is used for finding the cost of fencing or placing borders.

Area of Square

A square is a special type of rectangle where all four sides are equal. Formula: Area = Side2.

questionText: The present population of a city is 17,500. The population decreases by 12% in the first year and increases by 8% in the second year. Find the population after 2 years.
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Use the successive multiplying factor method for consecutive percentage changes:

Final Population = Initial Population × (1 - Decrease%) × (1 + Increase%)
Final Population = 17500 × (88 ÷ 100) × (108 ÷ 100)
Final Population = 17500 × 0.88 × 1.08 = 15400 × 1.08 = 16632
∴ The correct answer is 16,632.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Initial population of the city = 17500
⇒ First year percentage change = -12% (Decrease)
⇒ Second year percentage change = +8% (Increase)

Formula Used:
Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R1 ÷ 100) × (1 ± R2 ÷ 100)

Calculation:
⇒ Population after the first year = 17500 × (1 - 12 ÷ 100)
⇒ Population after the first year = 17500 × 0.88 = 15400
⇒ Population after the second year = 15400 × (1 + 8 ÷ 100)
⇒ Population after the second year = 15400 × 1.08 = 16632
∴ The correct answer is 16,632.

Additional Information
Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes multiple percentage changes in succession, the net percentage change can be computed as: Net Change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100.

Multiplying Factor Method

The most efficient way to compute final base values is by applying fraction multipliers: (1 + x ÷ 100) for an increase and (1 - x ÷ 100) for a decrease.

Base Change Principle

In consecutive changes, the new percentage operation always applies to the newly formed base (the result of the previous year), not the original starting base.

questionText: A solid wooden toy is in the shape of a right circular cone mounted on a hemisphere. If the radius of the hemisphere is 5.6 cm and the total height of the toy is 11.6 cm, then what is the volume of the wooden toy (in cm3 ) (rounded off to the closest integral value)?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the combined volume formula for a cone on a hemisphere: V = (1/3) × π × r2 × (2r + h)
Cone height h = Total height - radius = 11.6 - 5.6 = 6 cm.
V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 5.6 × 5.6 × (2 × 5.6 + 6)
V = (1/3) × 22 × 0.8 × 5.6 × 17.2 ≈ 565.07 cm3

Rounding off to the closest integer gives 565 cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 565 cm3.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total height of the toy = 11.6 cm
Radius of hemisphere (r) = 5.6 cm

Formula Used:
Volume of a Cone = (1/3) × π × r2 × h
Volume of a Hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r3
Total Volume = (1/3) × π × r2 × (2r + h)

Calculations:
⇒ Height of cone (h) = Total height - Radius of hemisphere
⇒ h = 11.6 - 5.6 = 6 cm
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (5.6)² × (2 × 5.6 + 6)
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 31.36 × (11.2 + 6)
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × 22 × 4.48 × 17.2
⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × 98.56 × 17.2
⇒ Total Volume = 1695.232 ÷ 3 ≈ 565.07 cm3
⇒ Rounding to the closest integral value, the volume is 565 cm3.
∴ The correct answer is 565 cm3.

Additional Information
Volume of a Hemisphere

V = (2/3) × π × r3, where r is the radius of the circular base.

Volume of a Right Circular Cone

V = (1/3) × π × r2 × h, where r is the radius of the base and h is the height.

Surface Areas

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a Cone = π × r × l, where slant height l = √(r2 + h2). CSA of a Hemisphere = 2 × π × r2.

questionText: In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90° and BD ⟂ AC. If AC = 9 cm and AD = 3 cm, then BD is equal to:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
By the Geometric Mean Theorem for a right-angled triangle:

Altitude to hypotenuse = √(Product of hypotenuse segments)
CD = AC - AD = 9 - 3 = 6 cm
BD = √(3 × 6) = √18 = 3√2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 3√2 cm.

Alternate Method
Given:
In right-angled ΔABC, ∠B = 90°

BD ⊥ AC

AC = 9 cm, AD = 3 cm

Formula Used:
In a right triangle, when an altitude is drawn from the right angle to the hypotenuse, the square of the altitude equals the product of the lengths of the two segments on the hypotenuse: BD2 = AD × DC.

Calculations:
⇒ DC = AC - AD
⇒ DC = 9 - 3 = 6 cm
⇒ BD2 = AD × DC
⇒ BD2 = 3 × 6
⇒ BD2 = 18
⇒ BD = √18 = 3√2 cm
∴ The correct answer is 3√2 cm.

Additional Information
Geometric Mean Theorem (Altitude Rule)

In a right-angled triangle, the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse divides it into two segments such that the altitude is the geometric mean of these two segments. (Altitude2 = Segment 1 × Segment 2)

Leg Rule of a Right Triangle

Each leg of a right-angled triangle is the geometric mean of the hypotenuse and the segment of the hypotenuse adjacent to that leg. (Leg2 = Hypotenuse × Adjacent Segment)

Pythagorean Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two legs. (H2 = P2 + B2)

questionText: Aman's average score in a series of tests was ‘y’. He appeared in one more test and obtained score ‘z’. If Aman appeared in total ‘n’ tests, then which one of the following expression shows his average score for all the tests?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Total number of tests taken by Aman = n.
Number of initial tests before the last one = n - 1.
Sum of scores in the first (n - 1) tests = Average × Count = y(n - 1).
Total sum of all n tests = Initial sum + Score of last test = y(n - 1) + z.
New Average = Total Sum ÷ Total Tests = [y(n - 1) + z] / n.
∴ The correct answer is [y(n - 1) + z] / n.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total number of tests appeared = n
Average score in the series before the last test = y
Score obtained in the last test = z

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations
Sum of Observations = Average × Number of Observations

First (n - 1) tests
Sum = y(n - 1)
Last 1 test
Score = z
Total n tests
Total Sum = y(n - 1) + z

Calculations:
⇒ Number of tests taken before the final test = Total tests - 1 = n - 1
⇒ Sum of scores in the initial (n - 1) tests = y × (n - 1)
⇒ Total score for all n tests = Sum of (n - 1) tests + Score in the last test
⇒ Total score = y(n - 1) + z
⇒ Required Average = Total score ÷ Total number of tests
⇒ Required Average = [y(n - 1) + z] / n
∴ The correct answer is [y(n - 1) + z] / n.

Additional Information
Average (Arithmetic Mean)

Average is defined as the sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Formula: Average = Sum of all terms ÷ Number of terms.

Combined Average

If group 1 has n1 items with average A1 and group 2 has n2 items with average A2, then the combined average is (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Net Change in Average

When a new observation is added, the new average can also be calculated as: Old Average + (Difference between new value and old average ÷ Total new number of items).

questionText: If the denominator of a fraction is multiplied by 2 and the numerator is increased by 2, the fraction becomes 1/2. If instead, the numerator is multiplied by 2 and the denominator is increased by 2, it becomes 6/7. What is the sum of the numerator and the denominator of the original fraction (in lowest form)?
solution:
Solution

Given:
Condition 1: Numerator increased by 2 and denominator multiplied by 2 = 1/2

Condition 2: Numerator multiplied by 2 and denominator increased by 2 = 6/7

Formula used:
Original Fraction = x/y

Sum = x + y

Calculation:
⇒ (x + 2) / 2y = 1/2
⇒ 2 × (x + 2) = 2y
⇒ y = x + 2
⇒ 2x / (y + 2) = 6/7
⇒ 14x = 6 × (y + 2)
⇒ 7x = 3y + 6
⇒ 7x = 3 × (x + 2) + 6
⇒ 7x = 3x + 6 + 6
⇒ 4x = 12
⇒ x = 3
⇒ y = 3 + 2 = 5
⇒ Original Fraction = 3/5

⇒ Sum = 3 + 5 = 8
∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questionText: If twice the son's age (in years) is added to the age of his father, the sum is 91. If twice the age (in years) of father is added to the age of the son, the sum is 119. What is the difference (in years) between the ages of father and son?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
When coefficients of variables are swapped, subtract the smaller equation from the larger one to find the difference directly.

⇒ (2F + S) - (F + 2S) = 119 - 91
⇒ F - S = 28
∴ The correct answer is 28 years.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Father's age = F years
⇒ Son's age = S years
⇒ F + 2S = 91   --- (Equation 1)
⇒ 2F + S = 119   --- (Equation 2)

Calculations:
⇒ Multiply Equation 1 by 2:
⇒ 2F + 4S = 182   --- (Equation 3)
⇒ Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 3:
⇒ (2F + 4S) - (2F + S) = 182 - 119
⇒ 3S = 63
⇒ S = 21 years
⇒ Substitute the value of S in Equation 1:
⇒ F + 2(21) = 91
⇒ F + 42 = 91
⇒ F = 91 - 42 = 49 years
⇒ Difference = F - S = 49 - 21 = 28 years
∴ The correct answer is 28 years.

Additional Information
Swapped Coefficients Rule

For equations like ax + by = c and bx + ay = d, directly adding them easily finds (x + y), and subtracting them directly finds (x - y). This heavily bypasses complex algebraic substitution steps.

Ages Problems Concept

Always assume the present age as a variable. Past ages are represented by subtraction (x - n) and future ages by addition (x + n). The difference between the ages of two people always remains constant over time.

questionText: If cot 18° = p/q, then the value of cosec^2(378°) / (1 + tan^2(378°)) is
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Reduce the angle to the first quadrant: 378° = 360° + 18°.

The expression becomes cosec2 18° / (1 + tan2 18°).

Using 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, it simplifies to cosec2 18° / sec2 18°.
Since cosec θ / sec θ = cot θ, the entire expression strictly reduces to cot2 18°.
Substitute cot 18° = p/q directly to get (p/q)² = p2/q2.
∴ The correct answer is p2/q2.

Alternate Method
Given:
cot 18° = p/q

Formula Used:
cosec(360° + θ) = cosec θ
tan(360° + θ) = tan θ
1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
cosec θ = 1 / sin θ
sec θ = 1 / cos θ

Calculations:
⇒ Angle reduction: 378° = 360° + 18°
⇒ cosec 378° = cosec 18° and tan 378° = tan 18°
⇒ Substitute into the expression: (cosec2 18°) / (1 + tan2 18°)
⇒ Apply the trigonometric identity 1 + tan2 18° = sec2 18°:
⇒ Expression = (cosec2 18°) / (sec2 18°)
⇒ Convert sec and cosec functions into fundamental sine and cosine functions:
⇒ Expression = (1 / sin2 18°) × (cos2 18° / 1)
⇒ Expression = cos2 18° / sin2 18°
⇒ Expression = cot2 18°
⇒ Substitute the given value cot 18° = p/q directly:
⇒ (p / q)² = p2 / q2
∴ The correct answer is p2/q2.

Additional Information
Trigonometric Quadrant Rule (ASTC)

In the first quadrant (0° to 90°), all trigonometric ratios are positive. Angles in the form (360° × n + θ) lie in the first quadrant, retaining exactly the original ratio and identical sign configuration.

Pythagorean Identities

The three fundamental identities mapping trigonometric pairs are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Key inverse and quotient relations include: cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ, sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ, and cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ = cos θ ÷ sin θ.

questionText: What is the area (in square units) of the triangle formed by the graphs of the equations: 2x - y + 8 = 0 and 8x + 3y - 24 = 0, and y = 0?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Put y = 0 to find the base points on the X-axis: 2x + 8 = 0 ⇒ x = -4 and 8x - 24 = 0 ⇒ x = 3.
The length of the base = 3 - (-4) = 7 units.

To find the height, find the y-coordinate of the intersection of 2x - y + 8 = 0 and 8x + 3y - 24 = 0.

Multiply the first equation by 4 to get 8x - 4y + 32 = 0, and subtract it from the second: 7y - 56 = 0 ⇒ y = 8.
Area = 1/2 × Base × Height = 1/2 × 7 × 8 = 28 sq units.
∴ The correct answer is 28 sq units.

Alternate Method
Given:
Equation 1: 2x - y + 8 = 0
Equation 2: 8x + 3y - 24 = 0
Equation 3: y = 0 (This is the X-axis)

A(-4, 0)
B(3, 0)
C(0, 8)
Height = 8
Base = 7

Calculations:
⇒ To find Vertex A, substitute y = 0 into Equation 1:
⇒ 2x - 0 + 8 = 0 ⇒ 2x = -8 ⇒ x = -4
⇒ Vertex A = (-4, 0)
⇒ To find Vertex B, substitute y = 0 into Equation 2:
⇒ 8x + 3(0) - 24 = 0 ⇒ 8x = 24 ⇒ x = 3
⇒ Vertex B = (3, 0)
⇒ To find Vertex C, find the intersection point of Equation 1 and Equation 2:
⇒ From Equation 1, y = 2x + 8
⇒ Substitute y in Equation 2: 8x + 3(2x + 8) - 24 = 0
⇒ 8x + 6x + 24 - 24 = 0 ⇒ 14x = 0 ⇒ x = 0
⇒ Substitute x = 0 to get y: y = 2(0) + 8 = 8
⇒ Vertex C = (0, 8)
⇒ The distance between A(-4, 0) and B(3, 0) is the base of the triangle.
⇒ Base = 3 - (-4) = 7 units
⇒ The height of the triangle is the perpendicular distance from C(0, 8) to the X-axis.
⇒ Height = 8 units
⇒ Area of triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height
⇒ Area = 1/2 × 7 × 8
⇒ Area = 28 sq units
∴ The correct answer is 28 sq units.

Additional Information
Area of Triangle using Coordinates

Area = 1/2 × |x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|
Distance Formula

The distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²).

Intercepts of a Line

The x-intercept is found by setting y = 0, and the y-intercept is found by setting x = 0 in the equation of the line.

questionText: An electric fan lists at Rs.265.80 and is sold at a discount of 10%. The shopkeeper gives a further discount of 8% for cash payment. The selling price of the fan, when payment is made in cash, is:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Using the multiplying factor method for successive discounts:

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 - D1)% × (100 - D2)%
SP = 265.80 × 0.90 × 0.92
SP = 265.80 × 0.828 = 220.0824 ≈ 220.08
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 220.08.

Alternate Method
Given:
Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 265.80
First discount (D1) = 10%
Second cash discount (D2) = 8%

Formula Used:
Selling Price (SP) = MP × [(100 - D1)/100] × [(100 - D2)/100]

Calculations:
⇒ Price after first discount of 10% = 265.80 × (100 - 10) ÷ 100
⇒ Price after 10% discount = 265.80 × 90 ÷ 100 = 239.22
⇒ Final Selling Price after further 8% discount = 239.22 × (100 - 8) ÷ 100
⇒ Final Selling Price = 239.22 × 92 ÷ 100 = 220.0824
⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, SP = Rs. 220.08
∴ The correct answer is Rs. 220.08.

Additional Information
Equivalent Single Discount

For two successive discounts of D1% and D2%, the single equivalent discount percentage is calculated using the formula: D = D1 + D2 - (D1 × D2) ÷ 100.

Marked Price (MP) vs Cost Price (CP)

Marked Price is the list price labeled on an item. All trade and cash discounts are exclusively calculated on the Marked Price, whereas profit or loss is calculated on the Cost Price.

questionText: Pabitra takes twice as long as Kader or three times as long as Rahim to complete a task. If they work together, they can complete the task in 2 days. How long will it take Kader to complete the task on his own?
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Ratio of time taken by Pabitra, Kader, and Rahim = 6 : 3 : 2
Efficiency ratio = 1/6 : 1/3 : 1/2 = 1 : 2 : 3
Combined efficiency = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 units/day
Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Time = 6 × 2 = 12 units
Time taken by Kader alone = Total Work ÷ Kader's Efficiency = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 days
∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Alternate Method
Given:
Pabitra takes twice as long as Kader and three times as long as Rahim to complete the task.

Let the time taken by Pabitra be 6x days.
⇒ Time taken by Kader = 6x ÷ 2 = 3x days
⇒ Time taken by Rahim = 6x ÷ 3 = 2x days
Method Used: LCM Method for Time & Work

Person	Days	Total Work	Efficiency
Pabitra	6x	6x	1
Kader	3x	2
Rahim	2x	3

⇒ Total efficiency = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 units/day
⇒ Total time taken working together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 6x ÷ 6 = x days
⇒ It is given that they complete the task together in 2 days.
⇒ Therefore, x = 2
⇒ Time taken by Kader alone = 3x = 3 × 2 = 6 days
∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Additional Information
Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If a person takes 'd' days to complete a work, their efficiency (one day's work) is 1/d.

Total Work Concept

Total Work is considered as the LCM of the individual times taken by each person. Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Total Time Taken.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If people work for the same number of days, their wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

questionText: In a Maths quiz 10 students scored 20 marks, six students scored 19 marks, five students scored 18 marks, four students scored 17 marks, and two students scored 12 marks. The average marks scored by the class (correct to 2 decimal places) is:
solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Use the Net Deviation Method by taking an Assumed Average = 18.
Net deviation = (10 × 2) + (6 × 1) + (5 × 0) + (4 × -1) + (2 × -6)
Net deviation = 20 + 6 + 0 - 4 - 12 = +10 marks
Average change per student = +10 ÷ 27 ≈ +0.37
Actual Average = 18 + 0.37 = 18.37
∴ The correct answer is 18.37 marks.

Formula Used:

Calculations:
⇒ Total students = 10 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 27
⇒ Total marks = (10 × 20) + (6 × 19) + (5 × 18) + (4 × 17) + (2 × 12)
⇒ Total marks = 200 + 114 + 90 + 68 + 24

Additional Information
Weighted Average

When data sets have different frequencies or weights, the weighted average is calculated as Sum(wi × xi) ÷ Sum(wi), where w is the respective frequency and x is the value.

Assumed Mean Deviation Method

A faster way to find averages involves picking an assumed mean (A), calculating total deviation (D) of all items from A, and finding True Average = A + (D ÷ N).

Combined Average

For two groups with sizes n1 and n2 and averages A1 and A2, the combined average is given by the formula (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

India’s persistent trade deficit remains a structural (1) __________ for policymakers, as the nation’s appetite for imported energy and high-tech components consistently outpaces its export growth, creating a cycle of dependency that is difficult to break. The heavy reliance on crude oil and gold imports creates a chronic imbalance that exerts downward pressure on the Rupee, complicating the Reserve Bank’s efforts to manage inflation without stifling growth. It is imperative that the government (2) __________ policies that move the economy toward high-value manufacturing and deep-tech innovation rather than relying solely on the services sector to bridge the gap. While the IT boom provided a temporary cushion, the long-term health of the economy requires a more robust base of physical exports. Failure to address this imbalance could lead to a widening current account deficit, threatening the long-term macroeconomic stability and the sovereignty of India's fiscal policy in an increasingly volatile global market.

Moreover, scarcely (3) __________ the domestic industry begun to adapt to global supply chain shifts when new geopolitical tensions disrupted the flow of critical raw materials, such as rare earth elements and lithium. This susceptibility to external shocks highlights the fragility of an import-heavy economy that lacks upstream integration. Unless the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative produces tangible results in the semiconductor and renewable energy sectors, the trade imbalance will continue to be a (4) __________ to sustained double-digit GDP growth, acting more as a drag than a stimulant in the global economic race. The path forward necessitates not just protectionist tariffs, but a genuine enhancement of domestic productivity and a significant reduction in the cost of logistics. Ultimately, India must transition from being a mere consumer in the global value chain to a pivotal node of production if it is to realize its demographic dividend.

Question:
What will come in blank (1)?
solution:
Solution
The correct answer is 'Quagmire'.

Key Points
The passage describes India’s persistent trade deficit as a "cycle of dependency that is difficult to break," emphasizing the complexity and the struggle of policymakers to manage it.
"Quagmire" (नाज़ुक स्थिति/दलदल) refers to an awkward, complex, or hazardous situation from which it is difficult to extract oneself. This perfectly fits the "persistent" and "structural" nature of the deficit described.
"Fillip" (प्रोत्साहन) refers to something which acts as a stimulus or boost. A trade deficit is a drain on the economy, not a boost, making this logically incorrect.
"Cynosure" (आकर्षण का केंद्र) is a person or thing that is the center of attention or admiration. While the deficit is a center of focus, it is not admired, and "quagmire" better captures the negative, trapped nature of the issue.
"Paradigm" (प्रतिमान) is a typical example or pattern. While the deficit is a pattern, "quagmire" is a much stronger descriptor for a "difficult to break" structural problem.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

The heavy reliance on crude oil and gold imports creates a chronic imbalance that exerts downward pressure on the Rupee, complicating the Reserve Bank’s efforts to manage inflation without stifling growth. It is imperative that the government (2) __________ policies that move the economy toward high-value manufacturing and deep-tech innovation rather than relying solely on the services sector to bridge the gap. While the IT boom provided a temporary cushion, the long-term health of the economy requires a more robust base of physical exports. Failure to address this imbalance could lead to a widening current account deficit, threatening the long-term macroeconomic stability and the sovereignty of India's fiscal policy in an increasingly volatile global market.

Moreover, scarcely (3) __________ the domestic industry begun to adapt to global supply chain shifts when new geopolitical tensions disrupted the flow of critical raw materials, such as rare earth elements and lithium. This susceptibility to external shocks highlights the fragility of an import-heavy economy that lacks upstream integration. Unless the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative produces tangible results in the semiconductor and renewable energy sectors, the trade imbalance will continue to be a (4) __________ to sustained double-digit GDP growth, acting more as a drag than a stimulant in the global economic race. The path forward necessitates not just protectionist tariffs, but a genuine enhancement of domestic productivity and a significant reduction in the cost of logistics. Ultimately, India must transition from being a mere consumer in the global value chain to a pivotal node of production if it is to realize its demographic dividend.

Additional Information
Current Account Deficit (CAD): A measurement of a country’s trade where the value of the goods and services it imports exceeds the value of the products it exports.
Downward Pressure: A set of factors that causes the value of a currency (like the Rupee) to decrease in the international market.
Stifling: Restraining or stopping something from growing or developing.

Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.
They plan to marrying in the spring.
solution:
Solution

The correct answer is Option 1)

Key Points
The phrase "plan to marrying" is incorrect in English grammar.
The correct form is "plan to marry," which uses the base form of the verb after "to."
In English grammar, after verbs that indicate planning or intention (such as "plan," "intend," "want"), use the base form of the verb (also known as the infinitive form) following "to."
Example: "I plan to travel next year."

The correct sentence is "They plan to marry in the spring.

Additional Information
Other options ("plans to marry," "plan to married") also have grammatical errors.
